findings.problem: The guide says a valid AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot may route provider observation while current write authority is independently denied, but TC-04 and GEV-02 simultaneously require lookup/provider-ledger counts to remain zero in that valid-snapshot/write-denial matrix. Provider observation necessarily exercises the observation lookup/ledger seam, so this oracle can only satisfy its zero-count condition by suppressing the very authorized observation needed to prove that observation authority remains usable yet grants no write authority. TC-07 has the correct shape by requiring zero admission/dispatch/create_ticket/effect while allowing observation, but GEV-02 makes the required release evidence contradictory.
findings.required_change: Separate provider-observation counters from provider-write/effect counters. For the valid-snapshot/current-write-denial rows, require the authorized observation lookup/ledger call and its ordered authorization-routing evidence to occur, while admission, dispatch, create_ticket and provider-effect/write counters remain exactly zero and snapshot provenance remains absent from every write-authorizer input. Align TC-04 and GEV-02 with that same differential oracle.

findings.problem: M4-78-AC-11 requires unavailable, timeout, malformed and not-found to remain distinct HTTP 202 non-terminal results. TC-06 injects those variants, but its pass oracle only requires 'Indeterminate/not-found remain distinct 202'. That permits unavailable, timeout and malformed/unknown to collapse to one undifferentiated result and still pass. The generic requirement for independent complete matrices in GEV-03 does not close the gap because no closed per-variant application/HTTP outcome or reason values are required by the oracle.
findings.required_change: Define an independently sourced closed TC-06 matrix with a separate expected row for unavailable, timeout, malformed/unknown and not-found. Require exact per-variant application result/outcome or reason, HTTP 202 status, unchanged non-terminal lifecycle, no retry authority, complete key set and recursive expected-versus-actual comparison so none of the four variants can collapse into another.

summary: REQUEST_CHANGES. v2 closes the prior authorized observation-order finding through the explicit authorization -> trusted routing -> provider-observation sequence and denial sentinels. The prior observation/write-authority separation finding is not yet closed because the required valid-snapshot/write-denial evidence contradictorily requires zero observation lookup/provider-ledger activity. Separately, TC-06 does not close AC-11's required distinction among unavailable, timeout, malformed and not-found non-terminal HTTP 202 outcomes. The remaining acceptance criteria, PostgreSQL-time fencing/takeover, crash-window recovery, SQLite/audit independence, verification commands and static-registry scope are adequately projected.
